solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ecstasy to take back when leaving City

indicators.note: leaving says the letters for the City go out of the longer word

parts.note: to recapture something is to take it back
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone finds bliss in reclaiming something once they walk out of the City.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, 'clubs' (C) leaves REAPTURE; the setter confirmed the clue should read 'leaving City', so EC, the City of London's postcode, comes out of RECAPTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is a state of intense delight, a synonym for ecstasy.

clue.text: Said to be placed in tall grass

indicators.note: in says the placed word sits within the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
put means placed

explanation.surface: Something said to have been set down among the tall grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed means generally believed or reported, so said to be.

clue.text: Heavy metal venue

definitions.meaning: the London ... is a famous theatre

explanation.surface: A concert hall for heavy metal music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' is not the music but a dense chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Palladium is a heavy precious metal and also the London Palladium, a West End theatre.

clue.text: Female relative, seen topless, let loose

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its top, its first letter in this down clue

parts.note: an auntie is a female relative

explanation.surface: An aunt seen topless has really let herself go.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie something is to undo its knots, setting it free.

clue.text: Loving learned book about Scottish island on loch

indicators.note: about means the book word is turned round

parts.note: a tome is a large scholarly book
Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A scholarly book, with affection, about a Hebridean island beside a loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TOME into EMOT, which is followed by IONA and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional means full of feeling, as loving is.

clue.text: Fugitive taking cover in eastern diocese

indicators.note: taking means the diocese word holds the cover word within it

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
a cap is a cover, as for a head or a bottle

explanation.surface: A runaway hides out under shelter in a church district in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' is a noun, a head covering, not the act of hiding; 'taking' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapee is someone who has got away from captivity, a fugitive on the run.

clue.text: Polish people news boss brings in

indicators.note: brings in means the editor letters take the people letters inside

parts.note: ED is short for editor
men means people

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor brings in Polish staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is the verb, not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and improve it, to polish it.

clue.text: Walton's advice perhaps succeeded for some percussion

parts.note: Izaak Walton wrote The Compleat Angler, so his advice might be to cast a net
S is short for succeeded in genealogy

explanation.surface: A tip from Walton led to success in the percussion section.
explanation.walkthrough: Walton is Izaak Walton, the 17th-century author of The Compleat Angler, not the composer William Walton.
explanation.definitionFit: Castanets are hand-held clappers, instruments of the percussion family.

clue.text: Annoy first wife after class in gym

indicators.note: after places the wife word after the class letters

parts.note: PE, physical education, is a gym class
Eve was Adam's wife, the first wife

explanation.surface: A first wife gets irritated following a gym lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To peeve someone is to irritate them, to annoy.

clue.text: Say why more attractive lover was sought?

parts.note: an ex is a former lover
a better-looking partner is sought when the old one was plain

explanation.surface: Explain why a better-looking partner was wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: The ex was plain: that is why someone more attractive was sought.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain is to give the reason, to say why.

clue.text: Scheme to involve one banking expert?

indicators.note: to involve means the scheme word takes the numeral inside it

parts.note: a plot is a scheme
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A plan to draw in a financial specialist from a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banking' is not finance: aircraft bank as they turn, and the one who does it expertly flies the plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot tilts an aircraft into banked turns, so the flier is cheekily an expert at banking.

clue.text: Stay out longer than you meant to?

definitions.text: Stay out longer than you meant to?

parts.words: Stay out longer than you meant to?
parts.note: staying out reads like a late night out, but 'out' here means asleep, unconscious past the alarm

explanation.surface: A partygoer stays out later than planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' means asleep, not away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversleep is to remain asleep, dead to the world, beyond the time you intended to wake.

clue.text: Blow having made deal without gain

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the deal word sits around the gain word

parts.note: having made a deal is having traded
to win is to gain

explanation.surface: Someone completes a transaction without making any profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so it signals a container rather than a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade wind is a steady wind, and 'blow' as a noun can mean a gust or gale.

clue.text: Stadium region to accommodate any number

indicators.note: to accommodate means the region word gives room to the number inside

parts.note: an area is a region
N stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A district builds a stadium to hold crowds of any size.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sport or spectacle, essentially a stadium.

clue.text: Go with current meaning

definitions.meaning: to be carried along by a current of water or air
the ... of an argument is its general meaning or gist

explanation.surface: Advice to flow with the tide, or with what is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Drift is both passive movement on a current and the gist or sense of what someone says.

clue.text: She dug the ground for Mytholmroyd poet

indicators.note: ground as the past of grind, so the letters are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman dug up the soil for a Yorkshire poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is not soil but the past of grind, rearranging SHEDUGTHE. Mytholmroyd is the West Yorkshire village where Hughes was born.
explanation.definitionFit: Ted Hughes, Poet Laureate, was born in Mytholmroyd in Yorkshire.

clue.text: Stand-off in centre of political power

definitions.meaning: in rugby the stand-off, or fly-half
... Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's residence

explanation.surface: A standoff erupts at the heart of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand-off' is not a confrontation but a rugby position: the fly-half, who wears shirt 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Number Ten names both the rugby fly-half's shirt and the Prime Minister's Downing Street home and office.

clue.text: Who's drummer to show virtuosity and spirit

parts.note: Keith Moon was drummer of the rock band The Who
to shine is to show outstanding skill

explanation.surface: A rock drummer shows off skills and soul.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine is illicitly distilled liquor, a spirit.

clue.text: Loudly threatened with undereducated displays

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The poorly schooled get shouted at.
explanation.definitionFit: To thunder is to speak loudly and menacingly, so thundered means loudly threatened.

clue.text: Variant mallard duck keeping one species protected

indicators.note: keeping means the rearranged letters hold the numeral inside them
a variant is a different version, so the letters of the bird are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A type of wild duck that keeps one of its kind safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variant' rearranges MALLARD to ARMADLL, and 'keeping' puts I in it to give ARMADILL before O. A duck is a batter's score of zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is an animal species shielded by a natural shell of bony armour, so literally protected.

clue.text: Built up a trick shot on snooker table area

parts.note: a massé is a trick shot in billiards and snooker, played with a steeply raised cue
the D is the semicircle marked at the baulk end of a snooker table

explanation.surface: A trick shot was built up on the snooker table.
explanation.definitionFit: Amassed means accumulated, gathered in quantity, so built up.

clue.text: Go diving in southern republic

definitions.note: scuba as a verb means to dive with breathing gear

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean republic

explanation.surface: An invitation to dive off a country in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: To scuba is to dive underwater using self-contained breathing apparatus, a form of diving.

clue.text: What makes soccer player score, leap and cry?

definitions.text: What makes soccer player score, leap and cry?

parts.words: What makes soccer player score, leap and cry?
parts.note: the letters of soccer player can be rearranged into score leap cry, and the device that does it is the answer

explanation.surface: What makes a footballer score, jump and shout with joy?
explanation.walkthrough: 'soccer player' and 'score, leap and cry' (without 'and') use the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranging the letters of one phrase to spell another is exactly what this wordplay device does.

clue.text: Expire in a uniform: farewell

indicators.note: in means the dying word sits within the other letters

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to expire is to die

explanation.surface: Dying while wearing a uniform is a final goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French goodbye used in English, a farewell.

clue.text: Neo is given long time to create impression

parts.note: Neo is the setter, so 'Neo is' becomes I'm
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: The setter is granted a long time to make an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or impression formed of someone or something.

clue.text: Ship in a sea in sight coming about in channels?

indicators.note: in means the whole group of pieces sits within the turned-around word
coming about, as a boat changes tack, says the word is read backwards

parts.note: to sight a gun is to aim it

indicators.note: in means the ship letters go within the other pieces

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A vessel in the sea comes about while in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming about' turns AIM into MIA, and the second 'in' puts ASSMED inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Channels, like television channels, are examples of the mass media, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Travel quickly to river after second

indicators.note: after puts to and the river letter after the second

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Speed off to a river after a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To motor is to drive or go fast, so travel quickly.

clue.text: Important aborigine not one to accommodate Jack

indicators.note: to accommodate means the shortened word gives room to the card letter
not means the numeral is left out of the aborigine word

parts.note: a Maori is an aboriginal New Zealander
I is the Roman numeral for one
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

explanation.surface: A key native figure who won't put up a jack.
explanation.definitionFit: Major means of great significance, a synonym for important.

clue.text: 20 past eight for food?

indicators.note: 20 refers to the answer at 20, which names a rearrangement, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Twenty past eight: is it time to eat?
explanation.walkthrough: '20' is the answer to 20 down, ANAGRAM, which tells you to rearrange 'past eight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a long thin pasta, an example of food, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Our moves keeping Juliet from Romeo as panellist

indicators.note: keeping means the two phonetic letters hold the shuffled letters between them

parts.note: J is Juliet in the NATO phonetic alphabet
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: moves means the letters of our shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Our moves keep Juliet away from Romeo, as in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' signals the anagram; the surface plays on Romeo and Juliet being kept apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A juror sits on a jury, a panel deciding a verdict, so is a panellist.

clue.text: Evidently no nudist's item of furniture

definitions.meaning: one who dresses, plainly not a nudist
a sideboard or chest of drawers

explanation.surface: Clearly no naturist owns this piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresser is both a person who puts on clothes and a cupboard with shelves for dishes.

clue.text: Attention brought to monk on line in Essex?

indicators.note: on sets the monk after the line, as one piece following on from another

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention
Dom is a title given to some monks

explanation.surface: Attention turns to a monk in Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is an English county, but also an earl's title, so the 'Essex?' is an earldom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of Essex holds a peerage, so Essex is an example of an earldom, hence the question mark.
